pairs.subject: llm-extracted-entity-graph
pairs.evidence: src/features/vault/shared/vector/tabs/ExtractTab.tsx:23 The Extract tab drives a per-document flat row extraction (kb_run_extraction -> kb_entities rows keyed by a fresh UUID, no relations, no cross-passage merge, entities not embedded into the vector index); searching the context for graph, relation and normaliz found no hits, so the graph-with-merged-nodes precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:309 Each extracted row gets a minted UUID. entity_key is only a display label, never a join key, so no surface-form identity decision is ever made.

src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:292 Every mention is a plain INSERT of its own row per document and run. Nothing merges a second passage into an existing node, so there is no merge operator to judge.

src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:153 One extraction call per document, with no further recall pass. The satisficing risk is real here, but the technique is scoped to graph building, so this is recorded as a proposal and not as a deviation.
src-tauri/src/engine/kb_extract.rs:155 Extracted rows land in one SQLite table only. No vector-index or graph-store fan-out exists for entities.

pairs.registryProposal: The recall failure (one pass returns a plausible handful, and truncated documents get EXTRACT_DOC_CHAR_CAP with no skip record) applies just as much to flat, schema-driven LLM row extraction with no graph. recall-passes-with-a-declared-cap may deserve a home that is not gated on building an entity graph (e.g. structured-output or a document-extraction subject).
